source.title: From Associations to Activations: Comparing Behavioral and Hidden-State Semantic Geometry in LLMs
source.authors: Louis Schiekiera; Max Zimmer; Christophe Roux; Sebastian Pokutta; F. Günther

record.tranche_reason: Uses cross-model consensus geometry as a reference baseline for its behavioral-readout analysis, but does not test whether alignment between independently trained models rises with scale or capability.
record.gate_note: The paper studies alignment between each model’s behavior-derived geometry and its own hidden-state geometry. Its cross-model consensus baseline is relevant to shared representation geometry, but the paper does not sweep model scale or capability, compare pairwise alignment as a function of scale, or test whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment. Results about forced choice versus free association are not results about convergence between models.
record.test_reason: The study's question is how well an LLM's own behavior (forced choice, free association) recovers its own hidden-state geometry. Cross-model consensus (the mean of the other seven models' hidden-state similarity matrices across all their layers) serves only as a benchmark reference and regression predictor, motivated by the Platonic hypothesis. The study does not vary scale or capability, compare pairwise model alignment, use vision models, compare seeds, fit mappings between models, or match features across models. It also does not test whether convergence survives other metrics or out-of-distribution inputs. The consensus numbers are an aggregate, layer-averaged reference, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The main conclusion is that forced-choice behavior recovers a model's hidden-state geometry substantially better than free association, adding signal beyond lexical baselines and cross-model consensus. Secondarily, the authors read the strong consensus alignment as consistent with a substantial common semantic subspace.
record.recipe_differences: Uses RSA, nearest-neighbor overlap, and regression on behavior-derived and hidden-state geometries; it does not reproduce either cited source’s method for testing convergence with scale.
record.method_sensitivity: Cross-model consensus alignment differs by hidden-state extraction strategy: mean RSA is r = .57 for Averaged and r = .79−.80 for the other three strategies; nearest-neighbor overlap also differs by strategy at k = 200 (.60 for Task (FC), .44 for Averaged).

fits_no_version.finding: Averaged over strategies, layers and models, the consensus of other LLMs' hidden-state geometry correlates with a target model's geometry at RSA r = .74. NN@k overlap rises from .51 at k=5 to .56 at k=200.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In 7–14B instruction-tuned LLMs, the layer-averaged consensus of other models' word-similarity geometry aligns substantially, but incompletely, with a target model's layerwise geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Consensus alignment depends on the extraction context: mean r = .57 under Averaged natural contexts vs .79–.80 under the prompt-based strategies, and NN@200 of .44 vs .60. Per model it dips as low as r = .25 for Qwen2.5-7B under Averaged (Fig. 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured cross-LLM similarity of word geometry depends on the context in which word hidden states are extracted.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: Only eight instruction-tuned models are included, and the cross-model result is based on consensus geometry rather than reported pairwise alignment by model size or capability. No scale or capability sweep is performed, and no analysis tests whether shared data or objectives account for the alignment. The study notes that its analyses are correlational.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; only aggregate cross-model-consensus results relevant to shared model geometry are recorded. The paper’s behavioral-to-own-hidden-state alignment results do not measure convergence between models.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep. The eight models span only 7B–14B, and alignment is never related to size.
No linear maps, stitching, relative representations or unpaired translation between models.
No feature or circuit matching across models.

Metric and input variation is applied to behavior-to-hidden-state alignment. Consensus alignment is reported under four extraction contexts, but only as a baseline, with no test of whether convergence depends on the metric or vanishes out of distribution.
No plateau analysis, and no test of whether shared data or objectives explain the alignment.

record.verdict_notes: Rows r1–r6 are correctly linked to none, and cannot_determine is appropriate because they are baseline reference values, not tests of a version. The consensus reference averages all layers of the other seven models, so it is not a pairwise or layer-matched convergence measure. The authors state their analyses are correlational.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure whether cross-model alignment rises with model size or capability.
No vision-language model comparison or paired image-caption representations.
Does not compare same-architecture networks trained from different initializations or measure shared features or subspaces across seeds.
Does not test mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired interchangeability between models.
Does not compare recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
Varies measures and inputs for behavior-to-hidden-state alignment, not for cross-model convergence. It does not test convergence under out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not test whether cross-model alignment plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives explain it.
